rationale: Reviewed against real cross-platform CI evidence for issue #94: PR #102, CI run https://github.com/SamuFL/RVRBoTron/actions/runs/34224039465 (macOS arm64 clang, macOS Intel clang, Windows x86_64 MSVC, float32 preset on all three; macOS arm64 and Windows x86_64 also on the float64 preset -- macOS Intel does not build the double preset, matching tail_tolerances_v2.json's own platform coverage), comparing every platform pair's compact modulation-v1-equivalence summary of the same millisecond-scale Feedback Loop Modulation tracer (tests/test_modulation_equivalence_cli.py) that carries a research-baseline Damping object too. Every exact-compared structural fact (modulationPresent, activeModulationCount, octave-band count, T20/T30 fit presence, withinPredictedTolerance, decay.withinAccuracyInvariant/significantDeviation, decayTilt.bandCount/significant, boundedEnergy.negativeTrend, each configured rate's own owner/rateHz/significant, and outputCorrelation.significant) reproduced exactly on every platform and precision. decayRt60Sec, decayRelativeError, decayTilt's slope/intercept, boundedEnergySlopeDbPerSegment, and outputCorrelation's two metrics all reproduced at the same scale tail_tolerances_v2.json's own equivalent entries document: same-architecture deltas at the 1e-16-to-1e-15 floor, float32 cross-architecture deltas up to ~1.6e-7 (decayRt60Sec, band=4000 T30) driven by the documented arm64 FMA-contraction divergence in the recursive shelf/delay-line arithmetic this analyzer's DSP output shares with tail-v2's, float64 cross-architecture deltas back down at the ~1e-14-to-1e-15 floor (a pure function of resolved.json's already-double-precision shelf coefficients for the predicted-RT60 entries, confirmed identical in magnitude at both DSP precisions exactly as tail_tolerances_v2.json's own float32/float64 entries observed). coherentPitchMovementBroadbandMeanMagnitude, coherentPitchMovementMagnitude and coherentPitchMovementRelativeMagnitude are new to this analyzer and behaved differently from every other metric here: at float32 their same-architecture delta (macOS Intel vs. Windows x86_64, both x86_64, observed up to 1350 out of a ~5.19e6 raw FFT magnitude for coherentPitchMovementMagnitude) was the SAME order of magnitude as their cross-architecture delta (up to 1920, arm64 vs. Windows). This is not the arm64-only FMA-boundary pattern every other metric in this file (and in tail_tolerances_v2.json) shows -- it means the instantaneous-frequency construction (analytic signal via FFT, unwrap(angle()), a phase derivative, a second FFT) is sensitive to ANY compiler's own float32 codegen choices for the underlying delay-line/shelf arithmetic, not specifically to arm64's default FMA contraction: unwrap(angle(...)) is a phase-unwrapping operation, and a perturbation as small as one ULP near a wrap boundary can flip a whole 2*pi turn in the unwrapped phase, which then propagates through the derivative and the second FFT as a much larger absolute change than the ULP that caused it. At float64 the same three metrics reproduced far tighter (coherentPitchMovementMagnitude's cross-architecture delta fell to 0.473, ~4000x smaller, consistent with a numerically sensitive but not fundamentally non-deterministic computation: doubling the DSP precision shrinks the perturbation that phase-unwrapping can amplify). Because same- and cross-architecture deltas were comparable for these three float32 metrics, their sameArchitectureAbsoluteTolerance is committed at the same order of magnitude as crossArchitectureAbsoluteTolerance rather than following every other metric's much-tighter same-architecture split; every other metric here keeps that split, matching tail_tolerances_v2.json's own documented reasoning. Each committed value below states its own observed evidence and headroom.

nonFiniteSampleCount.rationale: Observed: exactly 0 delta across macOS arm64, macOS Intel, and Windows x86_64 (CI run 34224039465) for the tracer's output.wav. A non-finite sample is a discrete numerical-hygiene failure, not a floating-point accumulation, same basis as every other tolerances file in this repository.

decayRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max cross-architecture delta 1.58e-07 (macOS arm64 vs. macOS Intel, band=4000 T30 fit, CI run 34224039465). The two x86_64 platforms differed by only 8.88e-16. Same basis and headroom as tail_tolerances_v2.json's own decayRt60Sec entry, reused unchanged: the identical octave-band T20/T30 fit machinery, imported rather than recomputed.

predictedTargetRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 4.01e-14 (macOS arm64 vs. macOS Intel, band=125, CI run 34224039465) -- identical in scale to tail_tolerances_v2.json's own observation for this same computation, a pure function of resolved.json's already-double-precision shelf coefficients, independent of DSP sample precision (confirmed here too: the float64 preset observed the identical ~4e-14 scale).

predictedRangeLowRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 4.02e-14 (macOS arm64 vs. macOS Intel, band=63, CI run 34224039465); see predictedTargetRt60Sec.

predictedRangeHighRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 4.82e-14 (macOS arm64 vs. macOS Intel, band=125, CI run 34224039465); see predictedTargetRt60Sec.

decayRelativeError.rationale: Observed max cross-architecture delta 1.47e-08 (macOS arm64 vs. macOS Intel, CI run 34224039465), while the two x86_64 platforms differed by 3.33e-16. A ratio of two decayRt60Sec-scale quantities; same basis as decayRt60Sec above and as tail_tolerances_v2.json's own entry.

decayTiltSlopeRatioPerOctave.rationale: Observed max cross-architecture delta 1.46e-08 (macOS arm64 vs. macOS Intel, CI run 34224039465), while the two x86_64 platforms differed by 3.12e-17. Derived from the same per-band T30 fits decayRelativeError uses, so it carries that entry's basis.

decayTiltInterceptRatio.rationale: Observed max cross-architecture delta 1.36e-07 (macOS arm64 vs. macOS Intel, CI run 34224039465), while the two x86_64 platforms differed by 1.11e-16. The same linear-regression fit's intercept term; see decayTiltSlopeRatioPerOctave.

boundedEnergySlopeDbPerSegment.rationale: Observed max cross-architecture delta 5.36e-07 (macOS arm64 vs. macOS Intel, CI run 34224039465), while the two x86_64 platforms differed by 4.44e-16. Same construction as tail_tolerances_v2.json's own eventualContractionSlopeDbPerSegment entry, reused unchanged.

coherentPitchMovementBroadbandMeanMagnit.rationale: Observed max delta 12.6 (macOS Intel vs. Windows x86_64, SAME architecture, CI run 34224039465), larger than the cross-architecture delta observed against macOS arm64 (up to 9.83) -- see this file's top-level rationale for why this metric's same-architecture divergence is not smaller than its cross-architecture one (a phase-unwrap amplification of ordinary compiler-codegen float32 differences, not an arm64-specific FMA effect). Committed at ~4.8x the larger observed delta, the same order of magnitude for both comparison classes rather than the tight/wide split every other metric here uses.

coherentPitchMovementMagnitude.rationale: Observed max delta 1920 (macOS arm64 vs. Windows x86_64, cross-architecture) and 1350 (macOS Intel vs. Windows x86_64, same architecture), both against a raw FFT magnitude of ~5.19e6 at the configured rate's own bin -- see this file's top-level rationale. Committed at ~4.2x the larger observed delta, the same order of magnitude for both comparison classes.

coherentPitchMovementRelativeMagnitude.rationale: Observed max delta 0.0407 (macOS arm64 vs. Windows x86_64, cross-architecture) and 0.0352 (macOS Intel vs. Windows x86_64, same architecture), against a baseline value of ~78.3 -- see this file's top-level rationale. Committed at ~3.7x the larger observed delta, the same order of magnitude for both comparison classes.

outputCorrelationMeanAbsoluteOffDiagonal.rationale: Observed max cross-architecture delta 2.55e-08 (macOS arm64 vs. macOS Intel, CI run 34224039465), while the two x86_64 platforms differed by 7.22e-16. A dimensionless [-1, 1] zero-lag correlation, the same construction diffusion_tolerances_v1.json already carries cross-platform headroom for at this same order of magnitude.

outputCorrelationMaxAbsoluteOffDiagonal.rationale: Observed max cross-architecture delta 2.55e-08 (macOS arm64 vs. macOS Intel, CI run 34224039465); see outputCorrelationMeanAbsoluteOffDiagonal (the pairwise maximum of the same correlation matrix, identical here since this tracer's matrix has a single off-diagonal pair).

nonFiniteSampleCount.rationale: Observed: exactly 0 delta between macOS arm64 and Windows x86_64 (macOS Intel does not build the double preset, CI run 34224039465); same basis as the float32 entry.

decayRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 2.81e-14 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64, band=1000 T30 fit, CI run 34224039465) -- the same tiny scale tail_tolerances_v2.json's own float64 decayRt60Sec entry observed, confirming the float32 preset's much larger delta is specifically a float32-DSP-build effect.

predictedTargetRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 4.01e-14 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64, band=125, CI run 34224039465) -- identical to the float32 preset's own observation, confirming this metric is independent of DSP sample precision.

predictedRangeLowRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 4.02e-14 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64, band=63, CI run 34224039465); see predictedTargetRt60Sec.

predictedRangeHighRt60Sec.rationale: Observed max delta 4.82e-14 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64, band=125, CI run 34224039465); see predictedTargetRt60Sec.

decayRelativeError.rationale: Observed max delta 2.81e-14 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64, CI run 34224039465); see decayRt60Sec.

decayTiltSlopeRatioPerOctave.rationale: Observed max delta 8.85e-16 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64, CI run 34224039465).

decayTiltInterceptRatio.rationale: Observed max delta 1.81e-14 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64, CI run 34224039465).

boundedEnergySlopeDbPerSegment.rationale: Observed max delta 1.06e-13 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64, CI run 34224039465) -- the same tiny scale as decayRt60Sec's float64 entry.

coherentPitchMovementBroadbandMeanMagnit.rationale: Observed delta 0.0031 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64, the only float64 pair available -- macOS Intel does not build the double preset, CI run 34224039465), ~4000x smaller than the float32 preset's equivalent delta, confirming this metric's float32 divergence is a precision effect amplified by phase unwrapping rather than a structural non-determinism (see this file's top-level rationale). Committed at ~6.5x the observed delta. sameArchitectureAbsoluteTolerance is set equal to crossArchitectureAbsoluteTolerance because no same-architecture float64 pair exists to observe separately, matching tail_tolerances_v2.json's own convention for float64 entries in the same situation.

coherentPitchMovementMagnitude.rationale: Observed delta 0.473 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64, CI run 34224039465); see coherentPitchMovementBroadbandMeanMagnitude. Committed at ~6.3x the observed delta.

coherentPitchMovementRelativeMagnitude.rationale: Observed delta 1.08e-05 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64, CI run 34224039465); see coherentPitchMovementBroadbandMeanMagnitude. Committed at ~6.5x the observed delta.

outputCorrelationMeanAbsoluteOffDiagonal.rationale: Observed delta 2.78e-15 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64, CI run 34224039465).

outputCorrelationMaxAbsoluteOffDiagonal.rationale: Observed delta 2.78e-15 (Windows x86_64 vs. macOS arm64, CI run 34224039465); see outputCorrelationMeanAbsoluteOffDiagonal.
